Stress & Adaptation

Stress — causes, general adaptation syndrome, coping and adaptation to illness.

🎯 After this chapter you can

  • Define stress and stressor
  • Describe the general adaptation syndrome
  • Explain coping and adaptation to illness

In simple words

Stress is the body’s response to any demand or threat. A stressor is anything that causes stress — illness, pain, hospitalisation, noise, worry.

The body responds through the general adaptation syndrome (GAS): alarm, resistance and exhaustion. Coping helps the person adapt.

General adaptation syndrome (Selye)

Stage What happens
Alarm “Fight or flight” — heart rate up, adrenaline
Resistance Body adapts; coping continues
Exhaustion Resources depleted; illness or burnout

Coping strategies

  • Problem-focused — tackle the cause directly.
  • Emotion-focused — manage the feelings (talk, pray, relax).
  • Adaptation — adjusting to a new health state (e.g., living with diabetes).

Nurse’s role

  • Identify stressors and help reduce them.
  • Teach relaxation — deep breathing, music, rest.
  • Support coping — listen, involve family, encourage.
  • Watch for exhaustion — burnout in patients and staff.

🔴 Exhaustion stage

Prolonged stress leads to exhaustion — illness, burnout or breakdown. Recognise early and support coping before it reaches this stage.

Where the nurse uses this

  • Identify stressors — pain, noise, worry, financial concerns, family issues.
  • Teach relaxation — deep breathing, guided imagery, rest.
  • Support adaptation — help the patient adjust to a new diagnosis (e.g., diabetes).
  • Watch staff burnout — encourage breaks, teamwork and support for colleagues.
  • Refer — refer to counsellors for severe stress or anxiety.

🔴 Most important for exams

  1. Stress is the body’s response to a demand or threat; a stressor causes stress.
  2. GAS stages: alarm, resistance, exhaustion.
  3. Alarm = fight or flight; resistance = adaptation; exhaustion = depleted resources.
  4. Coping: problem-focused (tackle cause) and emotion-focused (manage feelings).
  5. Adaptation is adjusting to a new health state.

⭐ Important for exams

  1. Relaxation techniques: deep breathing, music, rest.
  2. Prolonged stress causes exhaustion, illness or burnout.
  3. Support patients and families through illness-related stress.
  4. Nurses also need stress management to prevent burnout.

📌 Memory trick

GAS stages: “A-R-E” — Alarm, Resistance, Exhaustion. Remember “Are you stressed?”

60-second revision

  • Stress = response to demand or threat; stressor = cause.
  • GAS: alarm → resistance → exhaustion.
  • Alarm = fight or flight; exhaustion = depleted resources.
  • Coping: problem-focused and emotion-focused.
  • Adaptation = adjusting to new health state.

Test yourself

A stressor is:

Answer: B. A stressor is anything that causes stress — illness, pain, noise, worry.

The final stage of GAS is:

Answer: C. Exhaustion is the final stage, when the body’s resources are depleted.

Problem-focused coping means:

Answer: B. Problem-focused coping deals directly with the source of stress.

Exhaustion from stress can cause:

Answer: B. Prolonged stress leads to exhaustion — illness, burnout or breakdown.

Adaptation to illness means:

Answer: B. Adaptation is adjusting to and living with a new health state.
